title: Prescriptions & Renewals class register and entry conditions
content:
Linden Ridge holds every prescription of the Prescriptions & Renewals line in exactly one of six classes, ranked from the simplest to the most closely managed. The class is recorded on the prescription under its official name, and each class carries the entry conditions shown below.

| Rank | Class (official name) | Entry conditions of the class |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Acute Short-Course Prescription | the visit was completed the same day; the condition is self-limited |
| 2 | Standard Maintenance Prescription | the patient is an established patient; the condition is stable |
| 3 | Monitored Maintenance Prescription | the patient is an established patient; a baseline lab is on file |
| 4 | Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription | a controlled-substance agreement is signed; the state prescription-monitoring database (OARRS) has been checked; the prescriber is DEA-registered |
| 5 | Schedule II Controlled Prescription | a controlled-substance agreement is signed; the prescription-monitoring database has been checked; the prescription is transmitted by electronic prescribing for controlled substances; the prescriber is DEA-registered |
| 6 | Specialty Medication Prescription | the prescriber is a specialist; the payer's prior authorization is approved; the patient is enrolled with a specialty pharmacy |

### Reading the register

- Every condition listed for a class belongs to that class; a class is not described by only part of its row.
- The two controlled classes share three conditions (a signed agreement, a database check, a DEA-registered prescriber); only the Schedule II Controlled Prescription adds transmission by electronic prescribing for controlled substances.
- The Standard Maintenance Prescription and the Monitored Maintenance Prescription both rest on an established patient; the first adds a stable condition, the second a baseline lab on file.

### Lifecycle states a prescription of any class can show

A Prescriptions & Renewals prescription is recorded as prescribed, active, renewal requested, on hold, expired or discontinued. It becomes active when the signed prescription is transmitted electronically to the patient's pharmacy, moves to renewal requested when a renewal request is logged, to on hold when a renewal waits for a visit, lab, drug screen, agreement or prior authorization, and back to active when the renewal is approved. It becomes expired when its expiration date passes and discontinued when it is withdrawn, stopped or declined.
